source: JD-R model, Herzberg two-factor theory, Maslach Burnout Inventory dimensions; validated against IBM HR Analytics Attrition dataset (see ANALYSIS.md)

categories.label: Too much work, not enough time
categories.suggested_action: Audit current workload against team capacity; renegotiate scope or timeline with your manager before taking on new commitments.

categories.label: Unclear expectations or scope
categories.suggested_action: Request a written scope/definition-of-done from whoever assigned the work before continuing further.

categories.label: Friction with a specific collaborator
categories.suggested_action: Have a direct 1:1 conversation with the specific person about the friction before escalating; involve a manager only if that doesn't resolve it.

categories.label: Manager relationship or support gap
categories.suggested_action: Bring specific, concrete asks (e.g. more frequent 1:1s, clearer feedback) to your manager rather than a general complaint.

categories.label: Lack of recognition or visibility
categories.suggested_action: Start documenting your contributions and proactively share them in team/manager updates rather than assuming they'll be noticed.

categories.label: No growth path or skill development

data_signal.note: cluster of tenure/level/comp variables moves together; YearsSinceLastPromotion itself is weak (r=-0.033), so questions avoid literal promotion-timing framing

categories.suggested_action: Ask your manager directly what a promotion or scope increase would require, and get it in writing as concrete milestones.

categories.label: Micromanagement / lack of autonomy
categories.suggested_action: Propose a specific area where you take full ownership with periodic check-ins instead of step-by-step oversight, and track outcomes to build trust.

categories.label: Broken or frustrating tools/process

data_signal.note: proxy only; IBM dataset has no direct tooling variable

categories.suggested_action: File a specific ticket describing the friction and its time cost, and flag it in a team retro so it's prioritized against feature work.

categories.label: Work-life boundary being crossed

data_signal.note: shares strongest overall signal (OverTime) with workload_volume

categories.suggested_action: Set an explicit end-of-day/weekend boundary and name it out loud to your manager or team, rather than silently absorbing the overflow.

categories.label: Role doesn't match current skills

data_signal.note: training count is a weak proxy; questions framed around perceived fit, not training frequency

categories.suggested_action: Identify the specific skill gap and ask for either targeted training or a temporary pairing with someone who has it, rather than absorbing the mismatch silently.

categories.label: Accumulated technical debt slowing delivery
categories.note: engineering-specific; not represented in general-workforce HR dataset, theory-grounded only until repo-aware mode (Step 4) adds commit/ownership signals
categories.suggested_action: Schedule a scoped refactor spike for the affected module and pair at least two engineers on it before further feature work lands there.

categories.label: No clear owner for a critical system/module
categories.note: engineering-specific; validated in Step 4 via repo contributor-count signals, not HR data
categories.suggested_action: Assign an explicit owner for this system/module and record it somewhere discoverable (README, team wiki, on-call rotation).

categories.label: Review/deploy process is the actual blocker
categories.note: engineering-specific; validated in Step 4 via repo PR/issue-age signals, not HR data
categories.suggested_action: Measure time-in-review/deploy for recent changes and raise the specific stage causing delay in a process retro, with data attached.

categories.label: Critical knowledge lives in one person's head
categories.note: engineering-specific; validated in Step 4 via repo contributor-count signals, not HR data
categories.suggested_action: Schedule a knowledge-transfer session and require documentation or a second reviewer on that person's changes going forward.
